topPRs.title: op-deployer: add --deploy-mock-sp1-verifier to apply
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Since #23868, `op-deployer apply --deployment-target genesis` fails with `sp1Verifier must be specified for genesis deployments` unless the caller supplies a verifier. A dummy address in the `sp1Verifier` override doesn't help: `SP1PlonkAdapter`'s constructor reverts unless the address has code, and a generated L1 has none at that stage. The one working option, `DeployMockSP1Verifier`, existed only in the Go API, so sysgo and op-e2e kept working. Tools that run the CLI could no longer deploy a genesis devnet at all. kupcake is one of them, and it is what optimism-premium's devnet suites run on, so premium has held op-deployer at a commit from before #23868.

This adds a hidden, test-only `--deploy-mock-sp1-verifier` flag (`DEPLOYER_DEPLOY_MOCK_SP1_VERIFIER`) that sets the existing option. Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't set it. The existing check in `ApplyPipeline` still rejects it for live deployments, and an `sp1Verifier` override still takes precedence over the mock. The kupcake change that uses it, ethereum-optimism/kupcake#80, sets the env var, so op-deployer images without this flag ignore it rather than failing on an unknown flag.

`TestCLIApplyGenesisMockSP1Verifier` needs `forge-artifacts`, which weren't available where this was written, so its first run is CI's `go-tests` job, which passed. It runs a genesis apply through the CLI binary: without the flag it expects the existing error, and with the flag it checks that the mock is in the L1 genesis state. `go-code-reviewer` found no correctness issues, and its test suggestions are applied. `lint-go` (golangci-lint run on the changed packages, plus `go mod tidy -diff`) passes. No other review agent's trigger matches this diff.

topPRs.title: kona-gossip: record dial and connection counts as counters, not gauges
topPRs.author: syszery
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

<!--
A clear and concise description of the features you're adding in this pull request.
-->

`kona_node_dial_peer`, `kona_node_dial_peer_error{type}` and `kona_node_gossipsub_connection{type}` were recorded and described as gauges, but they are only ever incremented. This PR records them as counters, as suggested in #23699. Metric names are unchanged.

- Changed `gauge!(..).increment(1)` to `counter!(..).increment(1)` in `driver.rs` and `gater.rs`
- Changed `describe_gauge!` to `describe_counter!`, and adds the missing description for `DIAL_PEER_ERROR`
- `Metrics::zero()` now uses `.absolute(0)` for these metrics
- Doc comments updated, and the `dial_errors` test helper now reads `DebugValue::Counter`

Other increment-only gauges and related findings are noted in the issue.

**Compatibility**

The exported metric type changes from gauge to counter. The Grafana dashboards in this repo already query all three with `rate()`, so they should be unaffected. Owners of external dashboards or alerts might need to check theirs (for example whether they store the metric type).

**Tests/Verification**

<!--
Please describe any tests you've added. If you've added no tests, or left important behavior untested, please explain why not.
-->

- Searched the repo for every use of the three constants and metric names: all are in the gossip crate and the two dashboards, and nothing outside `rust/` references them. No gauge and counter should share a name anymore.
- Confirmed in the code that none of them is decremented or set to a non-zero value.
- `rust/` tests all pass on my machine, and `cargo +nightly fmt -p kona-gossip -- --check` is clean.

**Metadata**

<!-- 
Include a link to any github issues that this may close in the following form:
- Fixes #[Link to Issue]
-->

Addresses #23699

topPRs.title: ci: run 32 fault-proof tests at once in op-e2e-cannon-tests
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
**Metrics** (`op-e2e-cannon-tests`, develop only)
- Job: 52.7 min median (60.7 p95, 54 develop runs) -> 30.3 min median (28.2-36.7, 5 runs)
- develop pipeline: about 61 -> about 37 min
- Compute: about -44% per merge, on the same 2xlarge.gen2 runner

**Why**

The tests mostly wait on L1 blocks: 16 at once used about 3 of 16 cores, and per-test times are the same at 32. So the job takes about total test time divided by the number running at once. That number comes from `nproc` (`-parallel=16`), and the cannon tests are also capped by `OP_E2E_EXECUTOR_LIMIT` (16), so both go to 32.

**Why it's safe**
- The same 186 tests ran as on develop (180 passed, 6 skipped), with no reruns in 5 runs.
- Anonymous memory peaked at 22.3-23.5 GiB of 32 GiB in 3 sampled runs, including a point where every heavy test was running. No OOM kills and negligible memory pressure.
- A new step prints `memory.events` and `memory.pressure` after the tests, so an OOM kill shows up there instead of looking like a flaky test. If it does, lower the number.
- Local runs are unchanged.

**Tradeoffs**
- About 8 GiB of headroom. Heavier processes after a reth or cannon upgrade could use it up.
- CPU briefly saturates, and a few tests run 5-15% slower. `TestSuperCannonPublishCannonRootClaim` already needs a rerun in about 4% of develop runs, and 5 runs can't show whether that changes.

topPRs.title: kona-gossip: make block timestamp bound tests clock-safe
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
Fixes a flake in `test_block_invalid_timestamp_too_far`. The test builds a block at wall-clock second `t` with timestamp `t + 6`. `block_valid` then reads the clock again. If a second boundary passes between the two reads, the validator sees `t + 1`, so the block is exactly at the `current + 5` bound and is accepted. This failed on an RWX runner during the RWX CI pilot (ethereum-optimism/optimism#23151). With an offset of 10, the test fails only if more than 4 seconds pass. There is no effect on users. The production bound is unchanged.

`test_block_invalid_timestamp_early` (`-= 61` against the 60-second bound) is not racy and is unchanged: forward clock movement only pushes its block further into the past. Only a backward clock step could break it.

I did not inject the current time into the handler. That would let tests assert the exact `now + 5` / `now + 6` edge, but it is a larger refactor than this one flake needs. `rust-code-reviewer` ran on the diff: no findings beyond a comment-wording nit, which is applied.
